exercise.name: Flutter Kicks

reference.title: Flutter Kicks
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Hips, equipment Body weight, exercise type Strength

exercise.mechanics: Isolation (alternating hip flexion and extension, trunk held)

breathing.pattern: Breathe steadily through the kicks; do not hold the breath.

prescription.tempo: Small, steady kicks about 2 per second
prescription.progression: Longer sets, then lower legs (closer to the floor), then add a head and shoulder lift

cues.text: Lie flat, arms by your sides palms down, legs straight and together.
Brace and lift both heels a little off the mat; low back stays down.
Kick small and fast, one leg up as the other goes down; knees long, toes pointed. Keep breathing.
Bring the legs together and lower them to the mat under control.
Rest briefly and repeat the set.

mistakes.mistake: Low back arching off the mat
mistakes.fix: Raise the legs higher, put the hands under the hips, or bend the knees slightly.
Keep the kicks small (about a hand span) and steady.
Rest the head on the mat.

kinematics.norm: Heels lifted a little off the floor; lower is harder for the back (clinical opinion)
Small alternating kicks, about a hand span between the feet (clinical opinion)
Each leg moves a few degrees above and below the hold (clinical opinion)
Pelvis stays on the mat (clinical opinion; McGill 1998 for the load of straight-leg work)

sources.title: Andersson, Nilsson, Ma and Thorstensson 1997, abdominal and hip flexor muscle activation during various training exercises (Eur J Appl Physiol 75:115-123; PMID 9118976)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.

Straight-leg raises load the low back: leg raises gave higher psoas activity and spine compression than sit-ups in McGill's data (McGill 1998). If the low back arches off the mat, bend the knees or shorten the range.
Low-back pain or disc problems: prefer dead bugs or bent-knee alternatives.
Pregnancy and postpartum (diastasis recti): get individual guidance before dynamic trunk-flexion or straight-leg work.
modify: Legs higher off the floor (easier on the back).

muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas holds both legs up and drives each small kick. Leg raises gave the highest psoas activity in McGill's comparison (McGill 1998).
muscleNotes.hip_flexors_l: Iliopsoas holds both legs up and drives each small kick. Leg raises gave the highest psoas activity in McGill's comparison (McGill 1998).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and transversus hold the pelvis still while both legs are off the floor; bilateral (not unilateral) leg lifts needed abdominal activation (Andersson 1997).
muscleNotes.adductors_r: Keep the legs close and help flex the hip near the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.adductors_l: Keep the legs close and help flex the hip near the floor (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Keep the knees straight and the toes pointed.
muscleNotes.quads_l: Keep the knees straight and the toes pointed.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Brace against the alternating pull of the legs.
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Brace against the alternating pull of the legs.
